newsitem.title: USA: Protocol glitches enliven start of Denver summit.
newsitem.headline: Protocol glitches enliven start of Denver summit.

text.p: Leaders of the Group of Seven industrialised nations and Russia made a shambles of protocol as they started their annual summit on Friday, and it was mostly the fault of the summit host -- President Bill Clinton.
He was supposed to greet the guests as the other leaders arrived at the door of a 55-room Denver mansion for a dinner that was the summit's first official event.
A military honour guard snapped to attention as aides radioed orders to start the parade of arrivals.
Up swept a shiny black limousine with the first guest, Dutch Prime Minister Willem Kok, who is current president of the European Union, and European Commission President Jacques Santer.
But they had to cool their heels for nearly a minute until their host arrived, grinning sheepishly.
Not about to repeat his mistake, Clinton was on the doorstep waiting for the next guest, British Prime Minister Tony Blair, and Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi who followed him.
But he was missing again when Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto arrived, so the guest jumped out of his limousine and barged into the house without waiting for a welcome.
He and Clinton, laughing sheepishly again, came back out a few seconds later to pose for photographers.
Canadian Prime Minister Jean Chretien got a proper handshake as he arrived, and Clinton was waiting for his next guest, German Chancellor Helmut Kohl.
But Kohl arrived with his delegation aboard a bus that was unable to negotiate the winding driveway. They disembarked and walked the rest of the way.
"That's a huge bus. That is a full bus," Clinton said to reporters and photographers as he waited for Kohl to arrive.
"Helmut, you've got a whole bus!" Clinton laughingly exclaimed as he shook hands with the bulky German leader.
French President Jacques Chirac and Russian President Boris Yeltsin were the last two guests to arrive. By that point Clinton finally had the protocol in hand and greeted them properly.
